P.h: Critical Apache Roller RCE is under active exploitation, no login needed
P.p: TLDR InfoSec reports Apache Roller versions 4.0.0 through 6.1.4 have an unauthenticated deserialization flaw in the XML-RPC endpoint. Remote attackers can run arbitrary code, and exploitation is already happening in the wild.
P.s: Upgrade to Roller 6.1.6 or later. If patching waits, set enabledForExtensions to false in WEB-INF/web.xml, remove the xmlrpc servlet mapping and restart. Disabling XML-RPC in the admin UI does not stop exploitation on older versions.

items.h: PHP fixes seven critical flaws, including RCE paths
items.d: Depthfirst's phpAfterShell chains an arbitrary deserialization primitive with another bug to reach code execution. It hits any app on an affected PHP version using file-based sessions.

items.h: Java4Shell: OpenJDK AVX-512 Base64 RCE, CVSS 9.2
items.d: TLDR DevOps says it affects OpenJDK 17.0.6 and later on x86-64 and enables pre-auth RCE in Jenkins, Confluence and Tomcat. Upgrade OpenJDK or disable Base64 intrinsics now.

items.h: Ruby2Shell: one-byte heap overflow in Ruby
items.d: Single-byte encodings upcase the German sharp s as SS, but the loop checks for one. GitHub Enterprise Server, GitLab and other popular software are affected.

items.h: Rakuten Securities: data of 4.47M accounts may have leaked

P.h: Microsoft launches agent controls, a policy plane for AI agents
P.p: TLDR IT reports Microsoft introduced agent controls, a managed Azure service to define, manage and evaluate policies for AI agent behavior. It is built on the open-source Agent Control Specification and Agent Hooks.
P.s: It evaluates agent actions and content with safety classifiers, LLM judges and deterministic Rego rules, bringing runtime governance to mixed agent fleets without custom policy infrastructure. TLDR also notes Apple will warn macOS 27.3 users before granting agents control of their Macs.

P.h: Microsoft blames M365 outage on traffic mix missing from test labs
P.p: TLDR DevOps summarizes Microsoft's preliminary report on last week's M365 outage. It says the failure went undetected because the traffic mix and SKUs used in testing labs did not match production.
P.s: The linked analysis adds that throughput can vary by orders of magnitude with key skew, so load tests must mirror real traffic patterns to be valid. TLDR also covers Harness's comparison of seven flaky-test tools.
